speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You presented with a generalized nonpruritic rash, high fever, and a recent seizure. To narrow down the cause, were you exposed to anyone who recently traveled to a tropical region or has a rash?

speaker: Patient
text: 9-month-old infant. The patient is brought in due to a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash started on the trunk and spread to the extremities. Five days ago, the patient had a fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and experienced a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The infant was born at term, has no history of serious illness, and her immunizations are up to date. The current medication includes acetaminophen.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Roseola Infantum (Exanthem Subitum). The clinical picture of a high fever followed by a rash appearing as the fever resolves, in an otherwise healthy 9-month-old infant, is classic for Human Herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6) infection.
